lines: Jordan Rivera
+1 (555) 010-2287 | jordan.rivera@example.com | example.com/in/jrivera
EDUCATION
Northgate University | M.P.H. in Biostatistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Summit Climbing Gym | Front Desk Staff | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Checked in about 150 climbers a shift and sold day passes and memberships.
- Ran the weekend rental desk and logged gear inspections for the manager.
Meridian Heart Institute | Clinical Research Coordinator | Metro City, USA | Sep 2022 - Jul 2025
- Reduced data-entry errors by 70% by adding range checks and double entry for the primary outcome.
- Estimated median survival in each arm by averaging the follow-up time of patients who died, excluding censored patients.
- Built the enrollment tracker the three sites reviewed each week, flagging sites more than 10% behind target.
- Presented monthly safety reports to the data monitoring committee, and all 4 reviews passed without a protocol change.
- Established that the program was equivalent to usual care because the superiority test on readmission was not significant (p = 0.41).
- Coordinated a 3-site randomized trial of a nurse-led discharge program for 640 heart-failure patients, finishing enrollment 4 months early with 94% of follow-up visits completed.
Northgate University Hospital | Research Assistant | Metro City, USA | Jul 2021 - Aug 2022
- Screened 2,300 medical records for a diabetes cohort study, confirming eligibility for 410 patients against the protocol criteria.
- Interviewed 25 patients about missed clinic visits; the findings added text reminders that cut no-shows from 18% to 11%.
- Wrote the study's data dictionary for 180 variables, which the next two cohort studies reused.

- Cleaned and merged lab data from two hospital systems while also scheduling participant visits, ordering study supplies, taking minutes at lab meetings and covering the front desk, which resolved 1,200 mismatched patient identifiers.
PROJECTS
Asthma Readmission Analysis | Independent Project | R | Jan 2025 - Present
- Harnessed cutting-edge analytics to deliver transformative, patient-centered insights into respiratory health outcomes.
- Found that follow-up within 7 days was linked to lower readmission: 8.2% against 11.9% without it, after adjusting for age and insurance.
- Presented the analysis at the state public-health conference poster session.
Community Health Survey | Volunteer, Team of 5 | REDCap | Mar 2020 - Aug 2020
- Designed a 30-question community health survey and collected 1,100 responses, giving the clinic its first estimate of uninsured residents by neighborhood.
- The survey was translated into Spanish and piloted with 20 residents before launch.
- Ran a randomized discharge study of more than 600 heart-failure patients that completed enrollment months ahead of schedule.
SKILLS
Tools: R, REDCap, SAS
Methods: randomized trials, regression, mixed-effects models, survey design

items.says: The Community Health Survey dates conflict with the later coordinator-role dates if the two trial bullets describe the same study.
items.because: The survey is dated 2020, while the coordinator role describes a similar trial in 2022–2025.

items.says: Shorten the Summit Climbing Gym entry to one line.
items.because: Two duty bullets for a non-research role draw attention away from the research experience.

items.says: Move EXPERIENCE ahead of EDUCATION.
items.because: Several years of post-degree work establish the candidate’s direction more clearly than the degree.

items.says: The check-in and sales duties give neither an outcome nor context for the 150-climber count.
The rental desk and inspection-log duties do not state what the work accomplished.
The 70% error reduction has no baseline or comparison period.
items.because: The percentage is difficult to interpret on its own.

items.says: Averaging follow-up time among patients who died does not estimate median survival.
items.because: It gives a mean among observed deaths, while excluding censored patients discards survival information and can bias the estimate.

items.says: The survival line gives no estimates for either arm.
items.because: A reader cannot assess what the analysis found.

items.says: The meaning of the four reviews having “passed” is unexplained.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the reviews assessed or what “passed” means.

items.says: The review outcome is delayed behind the reporting details.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss it.

items.says: A nonsignificant superiority test does not establish equivalence.
items.because: Equivalence requires an appropriate analysis against a prespecified equivalence margin.

items.says: The readmission result gives a p-value but no rates or effect magnitude.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the practical size of the observed difference from the p-value alone.

items.says: The trial line does not specify the coordination work you personally owned.
items.because: The study outcomes do not show your individual contribution.

items.says: The trial line leads with the coordination role instead of its measurable outcomes.
items.because: The early enrollment and follow-up completion are harder to scan when they come later.

items.says: The patient-interview result should open this experience.
items.because: It connects patient input to a change in practice and a measured reduction in no-shows.

items.says: The data-cleaning result is buried after unrelated duties.
items.because: The long duty list dilutes the main contribution and may cause a scanning reader to miss the 1,200 resolved identifiers.

items.says: The line does not explain how the patient identifiers were matched.
The opening bullet makes broad claims without naming an analysis, finding, or supporting measure.
items.because: Its claims do not connect to the adjusted finding and conference presentation that follow.

items.says: The adjusted readmission finding should precede the current opening bullet.
items.because: Its comparison and adjustment factors give concrete evidence of the project’s result.

items.says: The readmission comparison gives no cohort size or adjustment method.
The survey bullet gives no key finding from the neighborhood estimates.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the estimate showed.

items.says: The translation and pilot details give no result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the pilot led to a useful change or what the preparation enabled.

items.says: Passive wording hides who translated and piloted the survey.
items.because: It is unclear whether you performed those tasks.

items.says: The discharge-trial bullet is unrelated to the survey entry and appears to duplicate the later coordinator-role achievement.
items.because: If it is the same study, the survey entry misattributes the work.

items.says: If this is a separate study, the line does not identify the discharge approaches or groups compared.
items.because: The survey entry otherwise gives no way to distinguish it from the later heart-failure trial.

items.says: “Months ahead of schedule” does not say how many months early enrollment finished.
The wording should make clear that the study, not the patients, completed enrollment.
